relevance_note: Case report of a girl with a de novo PSTPIP1 variant and PAMI syndrome ('a heterozygous pathogenic variant in PSTPIP1 (c.748G > A p.E250K)'), plus a literature table (Table 2) of 38 previously published PAMI cases with per-patient genotype and phenotype.
method_note: Read the whole paper. The index case (text plus Table 2 data row 1, 'Our case') is labelled 'patient' (rule 5); her two parents, tested negative for the variant, are 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2' (sex not stated). Table 2 (literature summary of PAMI cases) has no label column, so the 38 previously published people are 'Table 2 row 2' to 'Table 2 row 39' (row 1 = our case; the table's second header row is not counted). A short Python script transcribed Table 2 cell by cell from the Markdown; I checked its spans against the table and every span was verified verbatim. Conventions: 'Yes' = observed, 'No' = excluded (plain words, not symbols), 'Unknown' and 'Nil' = not reported. 'Hepato-splenomegaly: Yes' was mapped to both splenomegaly and hepatomegaly observed; 'Splenomegaly' in that column = splenomegaly observed only; 'No' hepato-splenomegaly (and the patient's 'no hepatosplenomegaly') does not exclude isolated hepatomegaly or splenomegaly, so those checklist items stay not reported. 'Cystic acne: No' does not exclude the broader acne checklist item. 'Abscesses'/'Sterile abscesses' (site not stated) and 'Osteomyelitis'/'Multifocal osteomyelitis'/'osteitis' (not stated sterile) were kept as feature rows but not mapped to the skin-abscess or sterile-osteomyelitis checklist items; only 'sterile osteomyelitis' was. Laboratory values in Table 2 (white cell count, CRP, zinc, calprotectin) are numbers without a stated normal range for the literature patients, so no elevated-marker, neutropenia, hyperzincemia or hypercalprotectinemia status was assigned from them. Literature-row zygosity and pathogenicity are not reported; variant class 'missense' and the pyrin-interaction functional statement were taken from Discussion sentences naming p.E250K and p.E257K; the gene for A230T/E250Q rows rests on the PAPA-variant sentence and the paper's PSTPIP1 framing (no gene printed in the table). Literature disease labels come from the Table 2 title ('PAMI cases'), except row 2 (Del Borrello text: 'a case of PAMI syndrome', with extra features and treatment from the Discussion) and row 11 (Khatibi: published as PAPA syndrome, which these authors think was likely PAMI). Contradictions/oddities: Table 2 lists Demidowich A230T and E250Q patients among 'PAMI cases', while the Discussion says these variants are associated with PAPA syndrome; the first author is spelled 'Del Borello' in the table and 'Del Borrello' in the text; Table 2 row 1 gives the patient a white cell count of 12.1 although the text reports persistent neutropenia; Table 2 rows 11 and 39 (Holzinger, Sampson) share identical WCC/CRP/zinc values (3.8, 146, 77); Hashmi et al. report 'a patient ... presenting neonatally with pancytopenia at birth' but the text does not say which of the two Hashmi rows (5 or 6), so it was not assigned. The patient's 'Full body MRI was normal' was not used to exclude any specific feature. Age at diagnosis is not stated (she was referred at nine weeks). n_patients_reported left null: the paper states no total of PSTPIP1-variant patients.
